title: Quotient of a regular ring by an element with a unit derivative is regular
statement: Let $R$ be a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], i.e. Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with $R_{\mathfrak p}$ a regular local ring for every prime $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $f\in R$ and let $D:R\to R$ be a derivation (an additive map with $D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)$) such that the image of $D(f)$ in $R/fR$ is a unit. Then $R/fR$ is a regular ring (if $f$ is a unit, $R/fR=0$, which has no primes and is regular).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PF (lemma-quotient-regular, line 11798) and its proof (reduction to R local; f not in m^2 by the Leibniz rule; Algebra Lemma Tag 00NQ lemma-regular-ring-CM)

proof.text: If $f$ is a unit then $R/fR=0$, which is regular vacuously. Otherwise let $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ be any prime of $R/fR$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be its inverse image in $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], $(R/fR)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ is $R_{\mathfrak p}/fR_{\mathfrak p}$. Thus it suffices, for every such $\mathfrak p$, to prove that this quotient is a regular local ring.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), applied in the reduction in More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PF

proof.text: Fix such a prime $\mathfrak p$. The derivation $D$ extends to $R_{\mathfrak p}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends]. The hypothesis that $D(f)$ is a unit modulo $f$ remains true after this localization: an inverse relation $aD(f)+bf=1$ localizes. If $f\notin\mathfrak p$, the displayed quotient is zero; otherwise $f\in\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ and $D_{\mathfrak p}(f)$ is a unit modulo $f$. If $f$ belonged to $(\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p})^2$, the Leibniz rule would put $D_{\mathfrak p}(f)$ in $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, contradicting its unit image. Hence $f\notin(\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p})^2$, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion] gives that $R_{\mathfrak p}/fR_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular local.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PF (lemma-quotient-regular), proof: reduction to a regular local ring, the Leibniz-rule contradiction for $f\in\mathfrak m^2$, and use of Algebra Lemma Tag 00NQ

proof.text: Since every localization of $R/fR$ at a prime is regular local by Steps 1 and 2, and $R/fR$ is Noetherian as a quotient of the Noetherian ring $R$, the regular-ring local criterion [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-local-criterion] shows that $R/fR$ is regular.
